text:
maria: Heads-up — acme-prod is reporting a mix of 401s and 429s after the quota rollout in us-west. Seen across a handful of routes. Sample response attached below. Can we triage?

akash: Which rollout ID / policy? I think we started the new burst-aware policy this morning at ~03:15 UTC as a 10% canary. Link: https://console/redwood/rollouts/rollout-2026-03-17

maria: Rollout ID looks like rollout-2026-03-17. Sample response from their SDK:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "auth/billing_required",
    "message": "Payment method declined for account acme-corp",
    "status": 401
  },
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d"
}
```
Also seeing 429s immediately after retries.

ryan: Noted. Can you paste request headers? Need to check rate headers and auth token. Also: did any billing jobs run around 03:10–03:20?

maria: Header snippet from their failing request:
```
Authorization: Bearer tok_abc123
X-RW-Quota: 100
X-Account-ID: acme-corp
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
```

jenna: We're seeing a correlated spike in 401 and 429 spikes for acme-corp in the observability dashboard. Traces show token validation failures followed by rapid client retries that hit the new burst window. Also: token-revocation job ran at 03:12 UTC (scheduled).

billing-bot: Automated alert: Invoice processing failed for account acme-corp at 2026-03-17T03:09:42Z — payment_source_declined. Invoice ID inv_98765.

akash: Ok that explains the 401 billing error. But the 429s are coming from the new rate policy enforcement that also factors in outstanding billing holds. The canary enforced a shorter burst window which made retries more likely to hit limit. We should consider toggling the canary to 0% for this policy while we sort the billing hold.

ryan: Agreed. Before rollback, let's collect a few more artifacts: full raw request/response for one user, and the token revocation job log. Jenna, can you attach the trace links?

jenna: Trace: https://tracing/redwood/trace/abc123. Log excerpt: "token_revocation: user_token tok_abc123 revoked for account acme-corp due to billing hold". Also captured rate-limiter metrics:
```
rate_limit.policy.rollout-2026-03-17: 10% active
rate_limit.enforced.burst_window_ms: 250
429 spikes: 150 -> 1200 RPS in 5m from acme-corp
```

maria: CS wants a customer-facing update. Can we do a quick mitigation: either whitelist acme-corp while billing holds are investigated or rollback the policy?

akash: I can flip the canary back to 0% now. Command:
```
# internal tool
redwood rollouts set --id rollout-2026-03-17 --percent 0 --reason "rollback for acme-corp billing-induced 401/429s"
```
I'll wait 2–3m for approvals. @ryan please confirm.

ryan: Confirm — prioritize rollback and whitelist if needed after rollback. Notify CS to tell customer we are pausing enforcement.

maria: I'll draft the customer note once you confirm rollback completed.

akash: Executed rollback at 03:50 UTC. Rollback ID rb_2026-03-17_01. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: Rollout rollback rb_2026-03-17_01 completed successfully (applied to policy rollout-2026-03-17).

jenna: Metrics are stabilizing — 429s from acme-corp down to baseline within a minute of rollback. Token revocation still needs CS/billing action.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll loop in billing and CS and follow up with acme-corp. tagging :eyes: :thumbsup:

ryan: Postmortem action items: (1) Add a preflight check for accounts with recent billing holds before enabling strict burst windows; (2) Add per-account emergency whitelist toggle exposed to CS; (3) Improve rollback runbook visibility.

akash: Will file a follow-up RFC for rollout gating and emergency whitelists.

maria: Closing this thread after CS update.
